pillar_reactions.evidence: Prospect played the whole pillar back accurately and unprompted: 'If I have it correctly, you mentioned about three to four times a week in terms of the mobility, strength routine, stretch on top of that, which is great. A lot of kettlebell fundamentals at first... and it'll be about a six-month window. Is that all?' No pushback on the month-one form-video phase or on intensity.

Tied the no-counting approach to a belief he already held: 'The what of food is very important to me. The counting food seems like it's not very sustainable. So I totally agree.' Also pre-agreed to change: 'When it will come down to making some changes to that, would you also be open to that?' - 'Yeah, yeah, I think I would.'

Volunteered a personal reason the community would work for him: 'I think seeing others, I'm very much team motivated. In a lot of the running that I did, I was on cross country teams... I enjoy when other people are kind of doing the same, sharing tips, ideas.'

anchors.raw: I have bought some at-home workout equipment that I'm enjoying as well. But because of that, I always am just poking around in terms of trying to explore and discover other at-home... workout opportunities.
anchors.note: He has already paid once for a self-directed at-home solution and is still self-coaching on it. The $6,000 is being compared against sunk equipment he already owns plus free TikTok research, which is how he found the programme in the first place.

anchors.raw: both of us have tried to do a lot of at-home workouts, because neither of us really liked the gym, but that's also an extra expense. So if we're not liking it anyway, we'd rather do it at home
anchors.note: The household reference point for fitness spend is a gym membership they deliberately cut as 'an extra expense'. That is the number in the room when 6k is quoted, and the rep never re-anchored against it.

anchors.raw: just in planning a wedding, we have a budget that we're working through
anchors.note: Not a competitor but a live claim on the same money, three months out from the wedding. This was the only stated blocker and the rep left it unexplored.

anchors.raw: She really likes the Peloton, like the bike Peloton at home.
anchors.note: The household already pays for a connected-fitness subscription. Mild, and the rep did not engage with it, but it sets the household's expectation of what at-home coaching costs per month.

unmet_demand.want: Meaningful visible change in the roughly three months before his late-September wedding
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme's own structure spends month one on light loads and form-video review, with intensity from month two - the rep said so directly - and is sold as a six-month arc. The prospect raised the timing twice and the rep twice deflected to the long term ('not a magic bill', 'it is just going to take a longer time') without ever stating what is realistically achievable by September.

unmet_demand.want: To know whether his fiancee could train alongside him, since she does the at-home workouts too
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep noticed the opening - 'it sounds like she might actually also start copying you if you start doing the kettlebells?' - and dropped it. No partner or household option was described, so a shared-benefit case that could have moved the exact person blocking the purchase was never made.
